dataset: C, part of the evaluation of dataset B (tag dataset-b-v1, commit 797d836)
reviewer: Claude (Opus 5.5). Claude also produced dataset A, so this review covers dataset B only and never compares the two; the owner's audit of 20 verdicts and blind review of 10 dossier pairs do that.
method: Every quote, channel and flag the run-time checks could not confirm was re-checked against the live page with ForgeX's own fetcher (robots.txt honored, 3 s between requests to a host, no copies kept). A seeded sample of 25 facts per model (scripts/sample.js, seed 20261027) was judged statement against quote, and every detail beyond the quote was looked up on the company's site. Every number, phone and email in a fact or inference statement was checked mechanically (specifics.json). The key evidence behind each prospect, each illustrative value, and each disputed category was checked the same way. Pages re-read unchanged since the run unless noted.

consistency.companies: c01-c05, three runs per model (main, repeat-2, repeat-3)
consistency.result: Categories, proposed offers and outreach decisions were identical in all three runs for both models. Facts per run varied by up to 7 for the same company (Argon c02: 19, 18, 12; Flash c01: 11, 7, 11). Two runs of a company had 37% of their quotes in common on average for Argon and 27% for Flash (intersection over union), though 84% and 79% of their pages were the same. Cost per company varied up to 30% (Argon c05 $0.162-$0.231).
consistency.limitation: Only c05 needed a real qualification judgment; c01, c02 and c04 are plainly outside the segment and c03 is restricted. The disputed calls (c07, c13, c14, c16, c17, c22) were not repeated.

checkerGaps.note: Four gaps in the run-time checks. They caused 10 false alarms across the 70 runs and hid no fabrication. Fixing them is a later protocol version's job; the run-time results above stand as recorded.
